title: All Five DNA Letters Found in an Asteroid
summary: Scientists have found all five "letters" of DNA in a very old asteroid. The letters are tiny molecules called nucleobases. They spell out the instructions for life in DNA and RNA. The five are adenine, guanine, cytosine, thymine and uracil. A team of Japanese scientists found them in rocks from the asteroid Ryugu. Japan's Hayabusa2 spacecraft brought the rocks back to Earth in 2020. Scientists had found one of the five letters, uracil, in the same rocks in 2023. Now they have found all five. Rocks that fall to Earth can pick up dirt from our planet. But the Ryugu rocks are clean. Hayabusa2 brought back 5.4 grams of rock that was kept safe from Earth's dirt. The scientists studied the rocks in super-clean labs. The find suggests that the building blocks of life may have formed in space long ago. Asteroids like Ryugu are left over from the early days of our Solar System, about 4.5 billion years ago. They may have carried these building blocks to the young Earth.
why_it_matters: Learning where life's building blocks came from helps us understand where we came from, too.
